Introduction to the reference

On this page
  • Saves, configuration and backups
  • Files, capacity and prepared output
  • Author content formats
  • Credits and compatibility

The reference section explains how Adorn and Adorn Seller Framework (ASF) store their data, which files belong together, and which limits affect your setup. Use it when backing up an installation, investigating configuration priority or packaging authored content.

If you are learning either mod for the first time, start with the Adorn introduction or ASF introduction. The task guides explain the workflow; the reference gives the supporting file and implementation detail.

Saves, configuration and backups#

Saves, config and backups separates shared setup from progress belonging to the loaded save. It explains Adorn Configs and Overwrite priority, where authoring creates files, and why a game save and its matching SKSE co-save should be preserved together.

Use that distinction before moving an installation or sharing a configuration. A seller setup and prepared voice output are not the same thing as a player’s order history, learned recipes or personal wardrobe.

Files, capacity and prepared output#

Files and limits identifies ASF’s drafts, recording sources, build manifests and final voice files. Prepared ESP, sequence data, provider information and audio describe a matching build and should stay together.

Adorn’s separate files and limits cover the assignment bank and sharing capacity. Assignment slots and ASF’s per-save craftable-piece slots serve different purposes.

Author content formats#

The riddle maker reference documents the content fields and JSON used for externally edited riddles. Keep stable entry IDs when updating a shared collection. The file format’s version identifies its schema, separately from the mod’s release version.

Credits and compatibility#

Artwork and credits identifies the supplied v4 wordmark and heading font used by this wiki. Compatibility and limits covers supported installation guidance, content requirements and capacity.

When asking for help, include the versions, steps, expected result, actual result and relevant logs so the problem can be reproduced.
